answer: A garden of agents stays honest when every identity must plant a costly, locked stake before it can trade: each account bonds funds that vest slowly and are slashed if peers catch it attesting its own sock puppets. Like a vine that can only grow one stem from each root, one stake supports one reputation; forging a sable-dark army of fake agents means paying the full stake for each, so the attack's cost scales linearly while its payoff stays capped by peer attestation weights.
